newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says crisis unlikely, but urges caution.
newsitem.headline: Manila says crisis unlikely, but urges caution.

text.p: Philippine Economic Planning Secretary on Wednesday said the country's economy is still on track, but cautioned against falling into the same traps that brought financial problems to Thailand.

"We certainly cannot afford to let our guard down. The trade and current account deficits must be constantly monitored. Our fiscal and monetary management must continue to be prudent to maintain short to medium term stability," Cielito Habito Habito said in a report to President Fidel Ramos.
Growth in the trade deficit growth slowed in the first quarter, while the current account deficit as a ratio to gnp has been steady at around 4.0 percent.
Monetary growth has also tempered, leading to a decline in the April inflation.
"It is not unlikely that we can do better than our six to 6.5 percent full-year projection (for inflation)," he said.
Full-year GNP growth target of seven to eight percent remained attainable despite a slowdown in the manufacturing sector.

The manufacturing industry is in a consolidation period, but the agriculture sector which grew an impressive 4.22 percent in the first quarter of the year could offset the lower industrial output, Habito said.
He also said the overall balance of payments was still manageable.
The Central Bank earlier said the surplus had shrunk to $450 million in the first four months of the year from $1.43 billion posted a year earlier.

"Even in the extreme (and highly improbable) case where fund managers cash in all their peso holdings, official international reserves are more than adequate to meet all of them. Thus, a balance of payment crisis is a rather remote possibility at this time," Habito said.

"Our optimism must be tempered with caution and persistence to stay the course of reform. On the other hand, being overly alarmist does not help any, and can only run the risk of being self-fulfilling and needlessly destructive," he added.
